title: Triage review of c33's phoretic swim-divide claim (SIMD) on fresh seed 7: capped Janus composites form from a uniform random particle mix and persist (S, I); labkit also reports travel and persistent splits, which I did not check track by track
summary: I re-ran the claimed world.py unchanged on new seed 7 with the claim's command (labkit, 800 frames, t=400, 128^2; rerun/seed7). particles.png: at t=0 A, B and food particles are mixed uniformly over the box; by t~50-100 the A particles gather into discrete round composites, many with a B cap on one side, and 17-28 composites persist to t=400 among free food particles. labkit: 363 tracks, 7 persistent; 63 long-lived tracks moved >= 1 body length, max 7.6 body lengths; 25 splits, 7 persistent, max generation 4, 42 merges (merge/split 1.68, reticulate). I did not run the claim's lineage.py swim-then-divide analysis, so I support only S and I.

observations.S: rerun/seed7/particles.png t=0: uniform random mix of A, B and food particles over the whole box; composites appear at scattered places by t=52-87
observations.I: rerun/seed7/particles.png t=104-400: 17-28 discrete capped composites persist among free particles (FACTS components final 17, 7 persistent tracks, longest 618 frames)

seeds_run.result: pass for S and I; M and D present in labkit metrics (max 7.6 body lengths; 7 persistent splits, generation 4) but not checked as one lineage

not_checked: M (labkit max 7.6 body lengths; not inspected per track)
D (7 persistent splits, generation 4, merge/split 1.68; lineage.py swim-then-divide not run)
verdicts.limitation: Triage only, one fresh seed, t=400. Merges outnumber splits (42 vs 25), so any genealogy here is reticulate; I did not check that the travelling composites are the ones that divide.
